content:
oncall-bot: Pager triggered — KV cache cardinality growth > 85% (service=rope-ingest, env=prod-eu) :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: Incident severity: P1 — potential customer impact; auto-creation of incident channel and page to oncall
Alex W: I'm oncall, ack'ing. grabbing metrics and recent deploys now
Devon K: saw spike at 14:12:20 UTC, continuous-batch-v2 rolled at 14:11:53. rolling window changed to sliding-window-size=4096 in that deploy
Maya R: logs show prefetch worker spawning many unique keys, KV hit-rate dropping and evictions skyrocketing
Jordan S: prod-eu-rope-2 showing kv_entries: 12k -> 3.9M in ~4m, mem_used -> 93%
Lee P: customers A & C reported 503s and elevated latency at 14:13. correlates with cache growth
Alex W: immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable prefix prefetch FF 2) cap batch size to 8 3) evict high-card keys 4) throttle long-context requests
Maya R: I can flip the FF. doing a quick canary to one host first
Maya R: (command) 
```
curl -X POST https://flag-api.internal/flags/prefetch_prefix -d '{"value": false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
Maya R: canary rolled to rope-2a host, no regressions in 30s
Devon K: applying batch cap via runtime config: set max_concurrent_batch_tokens=8 across router pool
Devon K: (kubectl) 
```
kubectl -n rope rollout restart deploy/rope-router --context=prod-eu
```
deploy-bot: Deploy triggered: restart rope-router in prod-eu by Devon K — rollout in progress
Jordan S: starting targeted eviction of high-card keys (prefix:longctx_*) using eviction tool. running with rate-limit 50/s to avoid thumping
Jordan S: eviction script output sample: 
```
[evict] scanned 1.2M keys, removed 1.05M keys, reclaimed 24GB
```
Lee P: after FF flip + batch cap + eviction: kv_entries down to 210k, mem_used -> 46%, p95 latency back to baseline within ~2m
Alex W: verifying customer impact window: 14:13 -> 14:21 UTC. customers who hit errors: A (enterprise-eu), C (saas-pro). Notifications drafted
Maya R: posting incident alert to status page and emailing affected customers; ops-runbook for rolling restarts attached
Devon K: root cause hypothesis: new sliding-window prefetch + continuous batching created pathological prefix cardinality, leading to KV cache explosion. rope scaling increased active contexts (NTK/YaRN windows) which amplified churn
Jordan S: mitigation notes: feature flag reverted, batch config tightened, eviction run, throttle on long-context routes applied. no infra scale-up needed thanks to eviction reclaim
Alex W: open postmortem items: A) add guardrails for max prefix cardinality B) autoscale for prefetch worker C) alert: faster kv-cardinality anomaly detection D) add canary test for sliding-window config changes
Lee P: creating follow-up ticket and assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml for model of prefetch heuristics
Alex W: handing off to night oncall (sre-rotation) at 16:00 UTC. current state: stable, low churn, no active customer errors, all mitigations in place. escalation path documented in incident ticket
sre-rotation: ack, taking over monitoring and customer comms. will run periodic eviction sweeps and watch mem/kvs for 4h
Alex W: final notes: keep FF off until we have guardrails and perf test. thanks everyone for fast turnaround :thumbsup:
Maya R: will schedule a replay + postmortem meeting, collecting logs and timeline for the writeup
Devon K: saving commands and snippets to incident docs: /internal/incidents/2005550000
Jordan S: leaving a short blameless note in the repo PR for continuous-batch-v2 to link this incident
Maya R: marking incident resolved in pager system after 30m of stability
